$comment: Shared dictation contract. Every client must reproduce each expected value from the same input. Catalog entries are referenced by {providerKind, direction, model} into the data object of shared/model-contracts/voice_catalog_contract.v2.json.

precheck: Count windows, not seconds: voiced windows = windows with value != null and value >= speechThresholdDbfs; fewer than minVoicedWindows (6) → no_speech.
Otherwise ok. too_short and no_speech show the no-sound-detected notice and do not upload.
silenceRuns: A run is a maximal sequence of windows with value == null or value < speechThresholdDbfs.
Keep runs of >= minSilenceRunWindows (8) windows; output [startSec, endSec] at window boundaries (index × windowSec), rounded to 3 decimals.
uploadFormat: Always m4a: the AAC-ADTS recording is repackaged to .m4a without re-encoding (passthrough). The v2 catalog lists only stt entries that accept m4a, so there is no per-entry format choice and no wav fallback.
segmentPlan: bytesPerSec = uploadBytes / durationSec (the m4a upload actually produced).

All segment boundaries (cuts, starts, ends) are rounded to secondsDecimals (3); comparisons use compareTolerance (durationSec − s > Lmax + 1e-9; a midpoint m is in the window when lo − 1e-9 <= m <= hi + 1e-9). From s = 0: while durationSec − s > Lmax, cut at the latest silence-run midpoint (rounded to 3 decimals) in [s + Lmax/2, s + Lmax]; with none, cut at s + Lmax. The rest is the last segment.
Segments are transcribed in order, one request each; the joined text is the result.
join: Text is handled as Unicode scalars (Swift unicodeScalars, Kotlin codePoint APIs) — never grapheme clusters or UTF-16 units — except insert offsets. Trim only the constants.text.whitespace set (no platform trim: U+0085 / U+FEFF are kept). Trim each segment text, drop empty ones, concatenate; insert one U+0020 between neighbours only when needsSpace(last code point of left, first code point of right).
needsSpace(l, r) is false when either side is missing or whitespace, either side is in noSpaceScripts, r is in noSpaceBefore, or l is in noSpaceAfter; otherwise true.
insert: Offsets are UTF-16 code units; the insertion point is max(selectionStart, selectionEnd) (Android selections can be reversed); neighbouring characters are read as scalars (codePointBefore / codePointAt). The transcript (trimmed) is inserted there; selected text is kept (never overwritten).
Add one space before it when needsSpace(char before, first char of transcript), and one after when needsSpace(last char of transcript, char after).
cursor = offset right after the inserted transcript (after the leading space, before the trailing space). Empty transcript leaves text and cursor (= selection end) unchanged.
failure: Transient = network error, timeout, HTTP 408 / 409 / 429 / >= 500. Auth = HTTP 401 / 403. Everything else is permanent.

attempt = 1-based number of the request that just failed. Transient with attempt <= maxAutoRetries: retry silently after Retry-After when present, else defaultDelaySec; Retry-After > maxRetryAfterSec (10 itself still retries) means no auto retry. input.failure.retryAfter is the raw header: only a non-negative decimal number of seconds counts; an HTTP-date or anything unparsable counts as absent; retry-after-ms is ignored.
When not retrying: primaryAction check_connection for auth, retry otherwise; the recording stays in the slot.
request: Parts in this order: model, then the language hint (only when the user picked a recognition language and the entry has languageField; the part name is languageField verbatim, value = ISO-639-1 primary subtag of input.language, which is the recognition language chosen in settings (one of the app locales; null = auto), after normalising _ to - and legacy codes in / iw / ji to id / he / yi), then file last (xai_stt requires file last; openai_transcriptions follows the same order).
No response_format part (json is the default for every P1 entry). Request URL = connection origin + entry path.

gemini_transcribe and dashscope_asr send JSON; their cases have expected {method, path, headers, json} and input.audioBase64 (the m4a bytes, standard base64) and input.apiKey (always "test-key"); expected.headers lists the auth header and Content-Type, and each client compares headers entry by entry. Auth header is decided by transport only: gemini_* use x-goog-api-key: <key>, all others Authorization: Bearer <key>; JSON requests also send Content-Type: application/json. gemini_transcribe body = {model, store: false, input: [{type: audio, mime_type: audio/m4a, data: <b64>}]} and never sends a language. dashscope_asr body = {model, input: {messages: [{role: user, content: [{type: input_audio, input_audio: {data: "data:audio/mp4;base64,<b64>"}}]}]}, parameters: {format: m4a}}; when a recognition language is picked and languageField == language_hints, parameters.language_hints = [ISO-639-1 primary subtag, same normalisation as above]. Allowed languageField per transport: openai_transcriptions / xai_stt → language; dashscope_asr → language_hints; gemini_transcribe → none. Mistral stt is plain openai_transcriptions multipart (unchanged shape). Old transports are byte-for-byte unchanged; unknown transports are dropped at decode.
response: Transcript = top-level string field text, trimmed. Missing or non-string text = invalid response (treated as a permanent failure). An empty transcript after joining all segments = no_speech.

input.transport selects the parser (absent = openai_transcriptions; xai_stt parses the same). gemini_transcribe: concatenate, in order, every steps[].content[] item with type == text, then trim; empty or no text = invalid response. dashscope_asr: output.text, trimmed; missing or non-string = invalid response. Invalid responses are not retried (same as today); retry classification looks only at the HTTP status, never at the error body.
retention: Pending files with age > pendingRetentionSec are deleted at launch (expired, not counted as lost). Discarding a recording longer than discardUndoAboveSec shows the undo toast; exactly 5 s does not.
liveDictation: System engine dictation listens live (E-244): Android pipe session (EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE, segmented session, EXTRA_PARTIAL_RESULTS) / iOS live analyzer; the AAC recording is still written for recovery. Cloud engines stay on the file path.

Live text = livePartial(finals, partial): finals are the segment results received so far, joined like join; partial is the current hypothesis, trimmed, shown as volatile (light #71717A / dark #8E8E96, E-263). One space between them only when needsSpace says so.

Recognizer callbacks → live state = liveResults(events) (E-364): text is trimmed with the constants whitespace set first. A non-empty final is appended to finals and clears partial; a non-empty partial replaces partial; an empty or null final promotes the current non-empty partial to a final (appended, partial cleared) and changes nothing when there is no partial; an empty or null partial changes nothing. SFSpeech sends the whole sentence again as a partial after endAudio and then an empty isFinal; appending the empty text would clear the words on screen, and only keeping the partial would still lose it at the next segment or when dictationOutcome ignores a leftover partial. The same rule applies to the text a segment contributes to the session result. Same on Android segment / onResults / partial callbacks (null text = empty); a recognizer error ending a self-record round (no match / speech timeout) is not a final and still clears that round's partial.

Writing into the message box = liveInsert: always recomputed from the text and selection captured when dictation started (never edited incrementally); same placement as insert (selection end, nothing deleted, needsSpace on both sides). region = the whole inserted span including added spaces (✕ removes exactly it and restores the original text); volatile = [cursor − volatile.length, cursor) in UTF-16. If the result would exceed maxLength (UTF-16, default constants.live.maxTextLength = 50,000, E-87), drop whole code points from the end of the live text, volatile first, then final, re-trimming and recomputing until it fits.

Done / ↑: stop the live session and wait at most constants.live.stopTimeoutMs (1500) for its final result, then dictationOutcome. File recognition is bounded by durationSec × fileTimeoutFactor + fileTimeoutBaseSec; a timeout is the condition timeout (busy). Android caches checkRecognitionSupport per (language, service) for supportCacheSec and creates a new recognizer only after the previous one finished destroy (S0 root cause).

dictationOutcome: every input states hasRecording (no default). live ended ok with non-empty finals → use them (a leftover partial is ignored), no file recognition — unless live.droppedAudio is true (the live session dropped queued audio, so words may be missing) and there is a recording: then recognize the file like any empty live result. Otherwise, with a recording, recognize the file once (busy auto-retry inside it); file text wins; if the file is empty or failed but text was on screen (livePartial(finals, partial).text, i.e. finals plus the last volatile) → keep it (source live_partial); else no_transcript / failed with the file failure kind. Without a recording (Android recognizer self-record) the live result is final and timeout → busy. A no_transcript code from the live session or from file recognition is reported as empty text (ended ok / {text: ""}), never as failureKind; failureKind is only one of the five kinds (cancelled and permission are handled before dictationOutcome).

After dictationOutcome: text → the live region is replaced by liveInsert(original, selection, [text], "") so the cursor ends after it; no_transcript / failed → the live region is removed (original text restored) and the card is shown; the recording is kept as today.
systemFailure: Classify every system recognizer failure with systemFailure (E-252) by the explicit table constants.systemFailure.codes; anything not in the table is other. iOS matches (domain, code) pairs, never the code alone. Sources (checked 2026-10-27): AOSP SpeechRecognizer.ERROR_* values; iOS SDK SFSpeechRecognitionTask.h error table (kAFAssistantErrorDomain / kLSRErrorDomain) and SFSpeechError.Code; NSURLErrorDomain = network (iOS network codes are not documented for Speech; S3 logs recognizer_code to confirm).

Pre-flight conditions are classified the same way: no recognition service (Android isRecognitionAvailable false / no enabled service, iOS recognizer isAvailable false or no backend available) → no_service; language not supported by the support check / supportedLocales (iOS: SFSpeechRecognizer(locale:) returning nil means the locale is unsupported) → language_unsupported; our own bounded wait expired → timeout (busy); user cancel → cancelled.

SERVER_DISCONNECTED (11) and kAF 1101 / 1107 are busy, not no_service: on the S0 Samsung the session was dropped before startListening because the service allows one concurrent session; a fresh recognizer recovers.

busy on attempt <= busyAutoRetries (1) with canRetry → autoRetry with a recreated recognizer (after the previous instance is destroyed), no card, no event. canRetry is true only for recognizing a saved recording (file); a live session or recognizer self-record passes false (retrying would lose what the user just said; its failure goes to dictationOutcome). attempt counts from 1 and restarts at 1 when the user taps Retry. cancelled → silent. permission → the existing permission card (open_settings), no failure event. The result always has all six fields (recreateRecognizer false and telemetry null when not applicable).

iOS hosts must assert the SDK raw values of every SFSpeechError.Code they map (noModel 4, assetLocaleNotAllocated 10, timeout 12, cannotAllocateUnsupportedLocale 15, insufficientResources 16) in a unit test, so a wrong number in this table fails on the device SDK, not only in JS.

Cards: title and body by kind (p2-copy voice_dictation_fail_*; other = existing 转写失败; no_transcript = existing 没有识别出文字 + voice_dictation_no_text_body); primary / secondary actions from constants.systemFailure.actions; failure cards use the error haptic.

telemetry: voice_dictation_failed with error_code recognizer (empty_transcript for no_transcript), failure_kind for the five kinds, recognizer_code = the platform integer code (omitted for conditions and for no_transcript), recognizer_domain = the iOS NSError domain if listed in constants.recognizerDomains of the telemetry fixture else other (iOS only), auto_retried = attempt > 1.

Voice conversation uses the same table for its system recognizer: no_transcript → sttResult with empty text (the reducer miss path, E-269), cancelled → nothing, busy on the first attempt → retry once, anything else → sttFailed.
